tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: the 1F grill serves curry (European-style roux), omurice, hamburg, fried shrimp, crab cream croquettes and cakes.
tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.vegan_detail: Not vegan: omurice, hamburg, seafood, curry.
tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.hours_raw: 1F Western grill and garden terrace: daily 11:00–21:00 (L.O. 20:00); closed at New Year (Tabelog). The 3F French restaurant Bois de Boulogne keeps its own hours (listed separately). 1F dinner bookings only; only the terrace open-deck table can be booked by day.
tokyo_hibiya_matsumotoro.notes: [Yōshoku · the restaurant inside Hibiya Park] A long-established Western-food restaurant set in Hibiya Park; this record covers the ground-floor grill and the garden terrace (the third-floor French dining room, Bois de Boulogne, is listed separately). The signature curry is a sweet, fruity, European-style Showa curry. Omurice comes with a choice of sauce and a side such as hamburg, fried shrimp or crab cream croquette. A shrimp and scallop omurice in tomato sauce was ¥1,850; a poulet, cake and coffee set ¥2,800, with seasonal fruit cakes shown at the table. The outdoor terrace is the joy of a fine day (paid special seats exist), and staff seated a party of 12 together. Expect a 30-minute wait at weekends or during park events; only the terrace open-deck table can be booked. Party plans with free-flow are about ¥8,500.

tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Omakase only, so swaps must be arranged with the chef. Nothing is called gluten-free; the course includes soy-sauce-marinated and shrimp-miso-soy-sauce red shrimp, tuna braised in miso, karasumi wrapped in mochi, and on some days soft-roe spring rolls with house XO sauce (2026 reviews).
tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: an omakase of fish and seafood, with clam broth and shrimp miso soup.
tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.hours_raw: Sushi daily 12:00–14:00 (last order 12:30; lunch only with a reservation made by 17:00 the day before) and 17:00–22:00 (last order 20:30) (Tabelog; official site). The official site lists closing days as irregular. From 22:00 to 04:00 the same counter runs as BAR末吉 (Bar Sueyoshi), with 60-minute all-you-can-drink at ¥3,000 (official site). Omakase courses only; seating 90 minutes, all-you-can-drink 60 minutes; arrive on time; seat-only bookings choose a course on arrival (Tabelog). Bookings by phone or online. Cards (VISA, Master, JCB, AMEX, Diners); no e-money or QR (Tabelog). 6 counter seats; non-smoking; private hire up to 20. Opened 3 July 2026 (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_sueyoshi_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, a six-seat omakase counter steps from the crossing] Opened in July 2026 on the ground floor a few steps from Roppongi Station exit 5: a single hinoki counter for six, omakase only, at a price unusual for Roppongi (¥8,800, or ¥11,000 with an hour of all-you-can-drink sake). The tuna is fresh domestic hon-maguro from まぐろ大善 at Toyosu, a dealer the shop's site says was founded 400 years ago (reviewers link it to Tokugawa Ieyasu), served as rare cuts like neck, cheek and tail; other fish come straight from fishermen around Japan, and you can watch videos of the buying and the tuna cutting as you eat. A course in autumn 2026 ran about 15 to 17 dishes: Nemuro hokke with fresh wasabi, tuna braised in two misos at the counter, karasumi in grilled mochi, smoked mackerel, red shrimp seared with shrimp-miso soy sauce, grilled eel, anago, tamago and brown-sugar ice cream. Diners in 2026 liked the chef's conversation, and one September party got talking with neighbouring guests; one September regular found the second visit less generous (sea urchin had become a ¥1,100 extra). At 22:00 the room turns into BAR末吉 until 4 am. Lunch only with a booking made the day before.

tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. Sushi with red-vinegar rice and many small dishes; the weekday lunch has an udon set and omurice with demi-glace (May 2026); soy sauce and miso are likely throughout.
tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog's listing ticks "vegetarian options" and "particular about vegetables", but no vegan dish is named; the menu is built around fish, sushi and sake snacks, and lunch comes with miso soup.
tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri lunch 11:00–14:00 (last order 13:30); every day 17:00–05:00 (food last order 04:00, drinks 04:30) (Tabelog). Lunch had paused and resumed in May 2026 (review). Cover charge ¥1,000 a person; private rooms add a ¥1,000 room fee (¥2,000 in all); karaoke ¥2,000 a person (Tabelog). 50 seats: counter, sofa and box seats, private rooms for 2, 4, 6 or 8; heated-tobacco smoking area (Tabelog; an April 2026 diner notes iQOS is allowed). tokyo_tsuyano_koku_roppongi.notes: [Sake bar · Roppongi, sushi and sake in a basement until 5 am] Down the stairs of a building facing Azabu Police Station, a minute from Roppongi crossing: a back bar lined with sake bottles, a counter, sofas, box seats with what one diner called a nostalgic snack-bar feel, private rooms and karaoke. The draw is the sake list, over 300 labels poured from 90 ml, in tasting flights or all-you-can-drink, served with red-vinegar sushi and small dishes until 5 am. A May 2026 group of three paid about ¥18,000 after a ¥5,000-a-head sake all-you-can-drink of some 30 labels (each guest must order a dish); others come after the last train or simply to stay till the first one. Courses with all-you-can-drink run ¥8,000–¥16,000. On weekdays it serves a cheap lunch: fluffy omurice, an udon set, and a seafood bowl limited to ten. An August 2026 reviewer says it is popular with celebrities and often used by the media for interviews. A ¥1,000 cover applies; English-speaking staff.

tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. Nigiri are seasoned at the counter (some pieces marinated or brushed with sauce, e.g. swordfish soaked a day in sake and mirin, October 2026), and the starters include squid shumai with ponzu (2026 reviews).
tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a fish and seafood counter; the course ends with a crustacean miso soup (October 2026).
tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.hours_raw: Sun–Thu and holidays 18:00–01:00 (last order 00:30); Fri–Sat 18:00–03:00 (last order 02:30) (Tabelog). A 10% late-night charge applies after 22:00 (Tabelog). Bookings online; arrival times in 15-minute steps (July 2026 review). 8 seats at an L-shaped counter (Tabelog; July 2026 review); non-smoking. Cards, IC cards, e-money and QR (PayPay, Alipay and others) (Tabelog). English menu and English-speaking staff (Tabelog). Opened 8 August 2024 (Tabelog).
tokyo_sushi_hajime_roppongi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, an 8-seat late-night counter on Imoaraisaka] A minute from Roppongi crossing, on the ground floor facing Imoaraisaka: eight seats at an L-shaped counter, open from 18:00 until 1 am, and 3 am at weekends. The young chef, from Saga and previously at Sushi Ryuta in Roppongi, serves an omakase of ten nigiri with sea urchin, two small dishes and miso soup for ¥7,700, or ¥11,000 with 90 minutes of all-you-can-drink sake and wine. The rice blends rice vinegar and red vinegar, the toppings are cut thick and the rice a little generous, on purpose, the chef told an October 2026 diner, because the course has few pieces. Autumn 2026 courses brought Shiogama hon-maguro, kasugo-dai, three sweet shrimp in one piece, grilled sanma, kinmedai and a purple sea-urchin gunkan; a monthly regular adds the Hajime roll of fatty tuna, salmon roe and eel. There is no kitchen, so starters are simple (July 2026). A September 2026 diner counted about half the guests from overseas; others use it as a second stop. A 10% late-night charge applies after 22:00.

tokyo_sougo_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask, at least two days ahead: the shop asks for allergies and dietary restrictions two days in advance and adjusts dishes (official site). Nothing is called gluten-free, and 2026 courses included fried spring rolls, corn fritters coated in arare, eggplant with somen, sushi in monaka wafers and a kadaif-topped salad; red miso soup and kombu tsukudani come with the rice.
tokyo_sougo_roppongi.vegan_detail: Shojin (Buddhist vegetarian) cooking. The English site says "Shojin vegetarian… (we can also cater to vegan guests)"; the Japanese site says vegan guests can eat with peace of mind. Say you are vegan when booking (two days ahead). Desserts and drinks include a "cream" zenzai and a ginger latte whose milk is not described; one March 2026 diner wrote that the course had fish, which contradicts the shop's own description.
tokyo_sougo_roppongi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat lunch 11:30–15:00 (last entry 14:00), dinner 17:30–23:00 (last entry 21:30); closed Sundays and public holidays (official site; Tabelog). 10% service charge on courses, food and drinks (official site). Private room for up to 7, room fee ¥5,000; semi-private room for up to 5, ¥2,000 (official site policy page; Tabelog). Cancellation fees apply (course: 100% same day, 50% the day before). Allergies and dietary needs two days ahead. Bookings via TableCheck, Tabelog or phone. 42 seats: 14 at the counter, tables, box seats, private and semi-private rooms; wheelchair access; designated smoking area; cards, no e-money or QR (Tabelog). Children welcome. Opened 23 February 2015 (Tabelog; the Japanese chef page also says 2015, the English page 2011). A second shop, 淡路宗胡, is at THE PASONA on Awaji Island (official site).
tokyo_sougo_roppongi.notes: [Shojin · Roppongi, modern Buddhist vegetarian kaiseki from a Daigo-family chef] Owner-chef Daisuke Nomura is the eldest son of the family behind 精進料理 醍醐 in Atago, where the chef was third-generation head chef while it held two Michelin stars from 2008 (official site). In 2015 the chef went independent and opened Sougo a minute from Roppongi Station to bring shojin ryori, the vegetarian cooking of Zen temples, to more people: traditional technique with modern touches and a few surprises, in a relaxed room with a counter, tables and private rooms. Dinner is a kaiseki course (¥15,400 or ¥18,700); lunch can be a ¥1,980 tray of seasonal vegetable dishes, rice and red miso soup, a shojin curry, or a lunch kaiseki. The menu changes about every three weeks; 2026 diners remember sushi in crisp monaka wafers, eggplant 'somen' and fried spring rolls, and you may take home the chopsticks and hand towel. The shop caters to vegans and allergies with two days' notice. A 2026 reviewer found the guests mostly from overseas and felt the staff might not understand much Japanese. Closed Sundays and holidays.

roles: Owner-chef (Tabelog: "Owner Chef Daisuke Nomura"; official site)

chef_bio.background: Per the official site: the eldest son of the family that runs the shojin restaurant 醍醐 (Daigo) in Atago, Tokyo; built a career as Daigo's third-generation head chef, with two Michelin stars from 2008; went independent in 2015 and opened Shojin 宗胡 (the English page says 2011; Tabelog gives 23 February 2015); teaches and promotes Japanese and shojin cooking in Japan and abroad; named to the Plant Forward Global 50. A second shop, 淡路宗胡, is at THE PASONA, Iwaya, Awaji (official site). A May 2026 diner had heard the restaurant is run by the son of Daigo's owner. Daigo itself is a hidden placeholder in this data (tokyo3_kamiya, name "精進料理 醍醐", address_ja "〒105-0002 東京都港区愛宕2-3-1 201").
chef_bio.philosophy: "I want to cook dishes enjoyable for all guests from every generation, every culture, and every diet… the most memorable dishes are those that give me the opportunity to share moments of gratitude with my guests." (official English chef page).
chef_bio.specialty: Modern shojin kaiseki; sushi in monaka; vegetable sashimi.

tokyo_taisei_yotsuya.notes: [Ramen · Yotsuya, a standing iekei counter at the station] A narrow standing-only counter right by Yotsuya Station's Exit 2, opened at the end of August 2025 as the second shop of Menya Taisei, whose first shop is in Nakano-Sakaue; one diner had eaten here back when the spot was Yokohama Ramen Ryoma. The bowl is iekei: a pork-bone and chicken soy-sauce broth, firm-to-order noodles, nori, spinach and thin chashu, and the house sign promises chicken and soy sauce. October 2026 diners found it refined for the style, strong on soy sauce but easy to finish, and best with a bowl of rice under nori dipped in the broth; the small rice comes with chopped grilled chashu on top. Opinions on the two shops differ: some find Nakano-Sakaue deeper and more chicken-forward, others prefer this one. Buy a ticket (cash only), hand it over, and the bowl comes in minutes; turnover is quick, but there can be a line at lunch and late at night. Hot in summer, cold in winter, and no hooks for coats.

tokyo_oliva_vava_yotsuya.notes: [Italian · Yotsuya, a third-floor hideaway with private rooms] Up steep stairs on the third floor of an old building a minute from Yotsuya Station, a room the shop says was inspired by a cosy restaurant where locals gather in Tuscany's olive groves: a bright counter on one side, tables and a run of private and semi-private rooms for 2 to 24 on the other. At night there are courses and party plans; on one, diners poured from bottles of red and white set by the table (October 2026). Staff ask about dislikes ahead and were flexible for a pregnant guest; one diner waited a while for water before anyone came (October 2026). tokyo_unicoco_yotsuya.notes: [Italian · Yotsuya, a restaurant devoted to sea urchin] "By uni maniacs, for uni maniacs": the owner-chef, a sommelier trained in Italian cooking, travelled Japan tasting sea urchin and opened this shop in 2016 after the summer-only uni festival at the chef's first restaurant, Osteria T, drew fans from around the country. It keeps 15 to 20 kinds of uni at a time, the site says, because the same species tastes different by season and even by beach, and every course turns on a tasting plate of 7, 9 or 12 kinds side by side, then uni pasta, a main and an uni dessert. Diners in 2025–26 compared red, black, bafun, purple and hadate uni, liked the rich ones from Aomori and Hokkaido and the uni from Hagi, and found uni even in the pudding; one parents' birthday got a surprise plate. A blue, sea-themed third-floor room with ocean-like glassware and private rooms. Not every visit landed: a November 2025 pasta lunch disappointed. Reservation only; the à la carte Italian next door, Oliva Vava, is under the same roof.

chef_bio.background: Per the official profile: born in Kagoshima in 1977; came to Tokyo at 26; at 31 enrolled at 辻調理師専門学校 in Abeno, Osaka; after graduating learned cooking and wine at an osteria in Shinjuku and qualified as a sommelier; in June 2012, at 35, opened Osteria T in Yotsuya, whose "夏限定ウニ祭" (summer-only uni festival) drew fans from across Japan; opened unico-co in November 2016 and reopened it after a refit in 2018 to host guests from around the world. The site says the chef tastes sea urchin around the country and joins each region's uni with its local ingredients and the chef's Italian roots. TV: 王様のブランチ (19 October 2019), ぶらり途中下車の旅 (6 February 2021), 全力!脱力タイムズ (9 July 2021), 食彩の王国 (23 July 2022) (official site). The house sake's Yamada Nishiki comes from the Tottori organic grower 杉山信一郎 (official site). The Italian restaurant Oliva Vava (tokyo_oliva_vava_yotsuya) on the same floor takes à la carte orders (official site).
chef_bio.philosophy: "ウニで世界一を目指す" — to be the world's best at sea urchin; keeping 15–20 kinds of a costly, perishable ingredient makes no sense for a restaurant, the site says, but it is worth the risk because guests are moved (official site).

tokyo_seki_tei_ningyocho.notes: [Izakaya · Ningyocho, Aomori seafood and obanzai upstairs by the crossing] A homely second-floor izakaya of 15 seats just off the Ningyocho crossing, built around fish and produce from Hachinohe in Aomori, and run by a chef from Hachinohe (per an April 2026 review). By day it is known for its "service" seafood bowl: about nine kinds of fish and shellfish heaped so high the rice disappears, with head-on red shrimp and baby scallops in the shell, for about ¥1,200, plus a free pot of fish broth to pour over the last of it as chazuke. Arrive before noon; seven people were already in by 11:45 one April 2026 day. At night it is a sake izakaya with daily obanzai, Aomori dishes such as senbei-jiru, Hachinohe mackerel and scallop skewers, and courses from about ¥4,000; a March 2026 diner counted around 100 dishes. Diners praise the value; one in September 2026 found the room worn, with a large TV on. Closed Sundays and holidays.

tokyo_mennosuke_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, garlic-salt "Gifu ramen" at a 10-seat counter] A small counter shop a few steps off the main road near Ningyocho station, opened in March 2025, serving what it calls original Gifu ramen. To order (by QR code) the cooks stir-fry pork belly, napa cabbage and cabbage in a pot, add the broth, then the noodles and garlic (October 2026), so the cloudy salt soup tastes of sweet vegetables, pork and a strong hit of garlic, with a ball of red chili paste to stir in at spice level 0 to 5. Diners in 2026 found it lighter than it looks; a Gifu native called it the long-missed taste of home, and an October 2026 diner described it as based on Gifu Tanmen, a local specialty of the Chubu region. Free bean sprouts and pickled mustard greens sit on the counter; most people add the half fried rice set. Expect a short queue at lunch; closed Sundays.

tokyo_a_la_bouteille_yotsuya.notes: [French · Yotsuya, a basement wine bistro under Yoshinoya] Down the stairs below the Yoshinoya on Shinjuku-dōri, a 20-seat bistro opened in 2017 that the shop says is a bistro for a first stop and a wine bar for a second. The cooking is prix-fixe French built on producers the staff have gone to meet: a mosaic terrine of the week's pesticide-free vegetables from Gori-san in Kiyosato, nerve-killed fish from Ishinomaki and Ise-Shima, game bought straight from hunters, and a sea bass in vine leaves and pastry with beurre blanc that has been on the menu since opening. Dinner starts with a black-truffle madeleine; the 5-course menu is ¥6,050, but supplements and a wine pairing can more than double it. About 100 wines, mostly French, and the owner-sommelier's pairings drew praise in 2026, with Greek Robola, a 100-year-old sherry with abalone and non-alcoholic pairings. Diners in 2025–26 call it a hidden spot that feels like a corner of Paris; solo guests eat at the counter, and one June 2026 diner heard that performers from Kioi Hall come here. Lunch only by booking; closed Sundays; ¥550 bread charge.

chef_bio.background: The official site says the shop opened in July 2017 "新宿西口Un Verreを経て" (after Un Verre at Shinjuku west exit), and calls the pâté de campagne refined in the way of "老舗レストラン出身のシェフ" (a chef from a long-established restaurant). The staff visit producers and buy only what they judge good, so they can pass on the producer's character and story; game comes direct from hunters, such as 儀間さん of Ashoro, Hokkaido, who sends only neck-shot deer; vegetables weekly from ゴリーさん in Kiyosato; prosciutto from 尾島博 (Hiroshi Ojima), maker since 1977 (official site; Tabelog menu). A June 2026 diner writes that "the owner kindly explained everything" and an August 2026 diner credits "pairings by the owner-sommelier". The site also sells the chef's French deli dishes online and a French osechi box (2026). No source names the chef or owner.
chef_bio.philosophy: "ワインも食材もこだわり、生産者の想いを伝える店でありながら、どこか気楽に" — particular about wine and ingredients, passing on the producers' feelings, yet somehow relaxed; a place where adults can take their time (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Kiyosato vegetable terrine; sea bass in vine leaves and pastry; game from hunters.

anecdotes.text: "I hear that performers and conductors from Kioi Hall often visit this place. Indeed, there were many signatures on the walls." — June 2026, post-concert gathering.

tokyo_odenya_den_yotsuya.notes: [Oden · Yotsuya, a basement oden counter since 1992] A small basement room on Shinmichi-dōri with one U-shaped counter for 15 around the oden pots, open on weekday evenings since 1992. Beside the classics (daikon, soft-boiled egg, konnyaku, beef tendon) come pieces that go into the pot when ordered and take 10 to 15 minutes: thick beef tongue, house tsukune and ganmodoki, fresh yuba, cherry tomatoes, Camembert, steamed onion, fried mochi, oysters in season, and a fukuro of vegetables and mushrooms. A diner on a fourth visit in December 2025 called it the best of the year and watched two cooks work the left and right pots. Finish with a lemon ramen or dashi chazuke. Calm rather than loud, good alone or with a friend; book or phone ahead. Closed weekends and all of August; smoking is allowed, and the toilet is up on an empty third floor.

chef_bio.background: No source names the owner or cooks. chef_bio.specialty: Oden in a gentle dashi; beef tongue and made-to-order pieces.

A February 2026 diner called it the local bistro worth keeping secret and paid about ¥6,000 with two drinks. Cash only; closed Sundays.

tokyo_manyoken_ningyocho.notes: [Ramen · Ningyocho, Hong Kong wonton noodles and dim sum by the station] A Hong Kong noodle and dim sum restaurant half a minute from Ningyocho station, open from 11:00 to 23:00 every day but Tuesday. Tabelog credits the cooking to a dim sum chef trained in Hong Kong with more than 40 years' experience. At lunch it is mostly noodles: plump shrimp wontons, chicken chashu and greens in a soy-sauce or salt soup, often as a set with freshly steamed shumai or har gow (¥1,550 in 2026), or slow-braised beef brisket on noodles or rice. At night the menu turns to dim sum, fried rice, congee and Cantonese dishes, with Shaoxing wine and Chinese teas. The shopfront looks small but the room runs deep, with booths and a counter for solo diners; an April 2026 diner heard Chinese spoken all around and felt abroad, and an October 2026 visitor came after seeing it on TV. No sets on Sundays and holidays; closed Tuesdays.

The menu page describes the wonton noodles as handmade wontons with springy noodles in a special soup. Opened 1 July 2021 (Tabelog). An October 2026 diner came after seeing the shop on TV.

tokyo_bangkok_peanuts_shokudo_ningyocho.notes: [Thai · Ningyocho, a back-alley Thai canteen open every day] A roomy Thai restaurant at the end of a narrow alley a minute from Ningyocho station, open for lunch and dinner every day of the year but New Year since 2012. The cook, per the shop's own site, is from Uttaradit and learned at Thai street stalls from the age of 15; staff greet you in Thai (October 2026). Lunch is the draw: a mini set of gapao and a curry over rice with a fried egg, salad and coconut tapioca for ¥900, or a green curry for ¥850 with ¥150 add-ons of mini gapao or tom yum noodles. One diner back for an eighth time in October 2026 has worked through Khao Soi, larb gai sets and beef-tendon rice noodles; another came for the khao man gai. At night it serves tom yum goong, grilled pork and chicken, som tam and stir-fries with Thai beers, and courses with all-you-can-drink. Diners find the heat mild and tuned to Japanese tastes; the shop says it will adjust spice and leave out coriander. Everything can be taken away. A September 2026 diner called the prices unbelievably low.

tokyo_kudan_ningyocho.notes: [Shabu-shabu · Ningyocho, a small hot-pot room where everyone picks a broth] An 18-seat shabu-shabu restaurant two minutes from Ningyocho station, where each diner gets a pot and chooses a broth: kombu, Japanese dashi, sukiyaki, medicinal, mala or soy milk, all on the house kombu-and-bonito dashi. The meat is sliced only when you order it (Black Wagyu and Iwate's Iwachu pork are the stars) and vegetables come from a self-serve bar. Dinner is a set with 120 g of meat from about ¥3,600 or an all-you-can-eat course from ¥5,650; diners in 2025–26 praised the marbled beef, with one finding the beef better than the pork. Weekday lunch is a small hot pot with help-yourself salad and rice for about ¥1,000. It fills up early: a February 2026 diner saw the owner or manager working alone and turning the OPEN sign round to keep up. A calm room, popular with groups; closed Mondays.

tokyo_sushi_kaminari_ningyocho.notes: [Sushi · Ningyocho, a young chef's 9-seat omakase counter] A bright nine-seat counter behind a double sliding door in a narrow Ningyocho alley, opened in December 2024 by Daiki Araki (named in a September 2026 review), who trained for ten years at Sushi Saeki and comes from a sushi family, per Tabelog. The chef's home ground is Himeji (official site), and the fish follows: Akashi anago, sea bream and cuttlefish alongside Toyosu catch and tuna from 石司. A course runs to six or seven small dishes, then about ten nigiri on red-and-black-vinegar rice, and ends with a toro-takuan roll and a castella-like tamago (¥27,000; Sunday lunch ¥16,000). Two repeat diners in 2026 note the rice changing and improving, and praise the chef's warmth; one August 2026 diner noted the shop carries the name of the owner's father. There are about 20 sakes, some from Himeji. Book through the shop's site; Sunday is the only lunch.

tokyo_kyushu_satsuki_roppongi.gf_detail: Ask. Nothing is called gluten-free. The menu leans on fried food (fried oysters, soft-roe tempura, assorted fried plates), gyoza, mentaiko motsunabe and sauce-dressed dishes, and horse sashimi is served with sweet soy sauce.
tokyo_kyushu_satsuki_roppongi.vegan_detail: Ask. Tabelog ticks "vegetarian options", and there are salads, bagna cauda and shishito, eggplant and shiitake skewers, but no vegan dish is named and sauces and broths are not described.
tokyo_kyushu_satsuki_roppongi.hours_raw: Daily 12:00–24:00, open all year including the New Year holidays (Tabelog); groups of six or more can ask about other hours. Online booking; same-day course bookings (June 2026 review); orders by tablet. 100 seats, all in rooms for 2 to over 30 behind roll curtains and shoji (June 2026 review); a smoking area, and 80 smoking seats per Tabelog. Cards, e-money and PayPay. English- and Chinese-speaking staff. Children welcome. Wheelchair accessible. Opened 19 August 2016 (Tabelog). A free whole cake for birthday and wedding after-party bookings (Tabelog remark).
tokyo_kyushu_satsuki_roppongi.notes: [Izakaya · Roppongi, private-room Kyushu izakaya for groups] Four floors above Sushi Sueyoshi, a few steps from Roppongi Station exit 5: a 100-seat izakaya made entirely of private rooms, open noon to midnight every day of the year. The menu is Kyushu comfort food — horse sashimi from Kumamoto, Hakata motsunabe with mentaiko, satsuma-age, charcoal-grilled jidori and yakitori from ¥83 a skewer — with shochu and sake, and most groups book a course with two and a half to three hours of all-you-can-drink for about ¥3,800–¥4,400. Diners in 2025–2026 call it a typical chain-style private-room izakaya: generous, fried-heavy and fine for a party rather than a destination; one in June 2026 found the curtain-and-shoji rooms noisy, another in September 2026 loved the chicken and pork hot pots finished as rice porridge. Tabelog counts 80 smoking seats. Staff speak English and Chinese. Gurunavi lists a second branch, 錦糸町店.

chef_bio.specialty: Horse sashimi; Hakata motsunabe; charcoal-grilled jidori.

tokyo_wagyu_yakiniku_tanjiro_roppongi.notes: [Yakiniku · Roppongi, all-you-can-eat wagyu by the crossing] On the fourth floor above Wendy's at Roppongi crossing, half a minute from the station: a bright, 60-seat yakiniku house with private rooms, open 11 am to 11:30 pm every day, built around two-hour all-you-can-eat courses of A4-or-better Kyushu black wagyu — 37 items for ¥3,980 Monday to Thursday, 55 for ¥5,980, or 65 with A5 cuts and steak for ¥7,980. The courses open with a heaping platter of meat; diners in 2026 praised the thick-cut tongue, outside skirt and horumon and found the value hard to beat for Roppongi, while one in September found a back table for six cramped and the loin disappointing, and one in July was told the limited tongue could no longer be held for a booking. An energetic manager runs a loud, cheerful room best enjoyed in a group. Heated tobacco is allowed in a smoking area; staff speak English and Chinese. Gurunavi lists a head shop, 炭治郎 渋谷本店.

chef_bio.background: Opened 17 April 2025 (Tabelog). Gurunavi lists a 炭治郎 渋谷本店 (head shop) with the same all-you-can-eat format. Reviewers in March and September 2026 describe an energetic, friendly manager.

chef_bio.specialty: Two-hour wagyu all-you-can-eat; thick-cut tongue.

Course bookings only (two hours); bookings from one person; from November 2026, à la carte seats on weekdays after 20:00 by same-day phone call, with a ¥2,000 charge for à la carte (Tabelog). 8 counter seats; non-smoking. tokyo_roppongi_kinme_sushi.notes: [Sushi · Roppongi, omakase with free refills in a basement counter] Down in a basement three minutes from Roppongi Station, eight counter seats and an unusual deal: a course of about 15 dishes, then as many repeats as you like of the nigiri on the blackboard, with all-you-can-drink included in most plans (¥10,000, or ¥15,000 with sake and Yamazaki and Hakushu whisky). The fish comes daily from Toyosu, some of it aged, on red-vinegar rice; courses mix sushi with small dishes like oysters, sea-bream carpaccio, a shark-fin chawanmushi and a sweet butter-soy inari. A regular writes that the chef earned a Michelin star in Italy and worked in Toronto, and sake lovers in 2026 enjoyed the chef's picks of unusual labels. Two diners in 2026 were too full from the course to order refills. The chef sometimes works the counter alone, and an October 2026 diner found the service curt. Opened November 2025.

An October 2026 diner was told on a Sunday that the shop closed at 14:00 that day — check before a weekend afternoon visit. Bookings accepted; QR ordering (August 2026). Fries and drinks are not included in à la carte burgers (June and August 2026). 26 seats including standing tables, all high tables and chairs; no strollers, children's chairs or kids' menu (Tabelog). tokyo_burger_revolution_roppongi.notes: [Burgers · Roppongi, 100% wagyu burgers with halal patties] A small burger and wine bar three minutes down Imoarai-zaka from Roppongi Station, across from Asahi Shrine. Every patty is 100% black wagyu with nothing mixed in, on a glossy branded bun; pay more and the same burger comes with Tokyo beef or Kobe beef, or with halal-certified wagyu; the shop says it draws tourists from Japan and abroad, and it is a walk from Azabudai Hills and Tokyo Tower. A plain black-wagyu hamburger is ¥1,780 and the classic ¥2,080; fries are extra, and diners in 2026 rate the truffle-salt fries and onion-ring fritters highly. The staff show you how to wrap the big burger in paper so it holds together, and a LINE sign-up gave one October 2026 diner ¥500 off. Lunch is usually busy, an August 2026 diner says; another came after seeing it on TV. High tables only, so no strollers.

chef_bio.background: Opened 30 October 2020 (Tabelog). The shop says its sauce is supervised by a Michelin three-star chef (no name given) and that it offers halal-certified Kobe beef; a March 2026 diner came after seeing it on TV.

chef_bio.specialty: 100% black-wagyu burgers; halal wagyu patties.
